slides.title: Module 1: Build Your First Robot — Lesson 1.1
bullets: Welcome to Autonomous Mobile Robotics (AMR)
Today's Goal: Unbox, inventory, and master mechanical fasteners
The Hands-on First Philosophy: Build First → Experience → Understand
slides.visual: Photo of complete Studica robotics kit with open storage bins.
slides.notes: Welcome students warmly. Emphasize that robotics is a hands-on craft. Today we start from zero: no coding yet, pure mechanical building.

slides.title: Hardware Spotlight: Structural Aluminum U-Channels
bullets: 6061-T6 Aircraft-Grade Extruded Aluminum
Standard 8mm Pitch Grid (holes spaced exactly 8mm apart)
High strength-to-weight ratio + internal wire routing cavity
slides.visual: Cross-section diagram of U-channel profile showing 8mm hole pitch.
slides.notes: Hold up a 240mm channel. Show how the open channel creates a protected tunnel for wires.

slides.title: Fastener Mechanics: M3 vs. M4 Sizing
bullets: M4 Socket-Head Cap Screws: 8mm, 12mm, 16mm lengths (2.5mm hex key)
M3 Button-Head Screws: for electronics decks and small sensors (2.0mm hex key)
Metric Rule: measure only the threaded shaft, NOT the screw head!
slides.visual: Fastener sizing chart showing M4x8, M4x12, M4x16 against a metric ruler.
slides.notes: Common mistake: students measure including the head. Demonstrate with a ruler that length is thread only.

slides.title: The Secret Weapon: M4 Nyloc Locknuts
bullets: Standard nuts shake completely loose in 10 minutes of driving
Nyloc nuts feature an integrated blue nylon locking collar
Vibration-proof: friction holds the bolt permanently in place
slides.visual: Close-up cutaway view of a Nyloc nut showing threads cutting into the blue nylon collar.
slides.notes: Pass around a standard nut and a Nyloc nut. Have students try to spin each onto an M4 bolt with fingers.

slides.title: Mandatory Laboratory Safety Protocols
bullets: Rule 1: ANSI Z87.1 Safety Glasses must be worn at all times
Rule 2: Never connect or disconnect battery leads with power switch ON
Rule 3: Tie back long hair, remove lanyard badges, roll up loose sleeves
slides.visual: Icons for Eye Protection, Battery Safety, and Hair Restraint.
slides.notes: Non-negotiable. Enforce eye protection before anyone opens a tool bin.

slides.title: Troubleshooting: Cross-Threading & Stripped Screws
bullets: If a bolt feels stiff after 1-2 turns: STOP! Do not force it
Use the Back-Turn Rule: turn counter-clockwise until you feel a gentle click
Always align the hex wrench 90° straight into the socket
slides.visual: Side-by-side illustration: Cross-threaded screw (tilted) vs properly aligned perpendicular screw.
slides.notes: Demonstrate the back-turn technique. Explain that aluminum is softer than steel and threads can be ruined if forced.

slides.title: Junior Hands-On Challenge: The Rigidity Squeeze
bullets: Assemble a 4-beam square test frame with corner gussets and Nyloc nuts
Hold opposite corners and apply torsional twist
Target: Zero play, zero wobble, zero clicking sound!
slides.visual: Hands grasping opposite corners of a square aluminum test frame.
slides.notes: Walk around the lab and test student frames. If it clicks or flexes, guide them to tighten loose bolts.

slides.title: Exit Ticket & Lab Wrap-Up
bullets: Q1: What does the blue nylon collar inside a Nyloc nut do?
Q2: Why do we never use standard hex nuts on motor mounts?
Q3: Name the 3 mandatory lab safety rules.
Tool accounting: return hex keys and rulers to bin
slides.visual: Exit ticket checkmark icon and lab cleanup reminder.
slides.notes: Ensure all tools are accounted for before dismissing class. Review Exit Ticket submissions.

slides.title: Understanding the Robot Controller
bullets: How your robot thinks, reacts, and drives
The Dual-Brain Architecture: Linux vs. FPGA
The CAN Bus Network: High-speed motor telemetry
slides.visual: Block diagram of Raspberry Pi 4, VMX-pi FPGA, and Titan Quad Controller.
slides.notes: Introduce the analogy: Raspberry Pi = Cerebral Cortex, VMX-pi = Spinal Cord Reflexes, Titan = Muscles.

slides.title: High-Level Brain: Raspberry Pi 4
bullets: Runs Ubuntu Linux 22.04 LTS and ROS 2 Humble
Processes complex LiDAR maps, cameras, and Wi-Fi teleop
Non-deterministic: background OS tasks can jitter motor timing
slides.visual: Raspberry Pi 4 board with Ethernet, USB 3.0, and quad-core CPU.
slides.notes: Explain why Linux is great for AI and maps, but bad for timing individual motor pulses.

slides.title: Real-Time Reflexes: VMX-pi FPGA & navX IMU
bullets: Dedicated FPGA hardware for microsecond timing
Integrated 9-Axis navX Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU)
Deterministic hardware interrupts and high-speed encoder counters
slides.visual: VMX-pi circuit board layout showing FPGA chip and IMU sensor.
slides.notes: Explain that an FPGA runs in pure silicon gates—timing is exact to the microsecond.

slides.title: The Muscle: Titan Quad Motor Controller
bullets: 4-Channel H-Bridge motor amplifier (12V DC, 20A peak)
Communicates over 1 Mbps differential Controller Area Network (CAN)
Hardware closed-loop velocity PID and encoder tracking
slides.visual: Titan Quad Controller with 4 motor channels and CAN Weidmuller port.
slides.notes: Titan handles the heavy currents so the Raspberry Pi never experiences motor surges.

slides.title: Twisted Pair CAN Bus Physics
bullets: Yellow (CAN_H) and Green (CAN_L) wires twisted tightly
Differential signaling cancels high-current motor EMI noise
Crucial: 120-ohm terminating resistor switch must be ON
slides.visual: Differential voltage waveform diagram showing noise cancellation.
slides.notes: Demonstrate the 120-ohm termination switch. Explain signal echoes if termination is missing.

slides.title: VMX-pi Header Geography
bullets: HiCurrDIO (Ch 20-23): 1.0A sink for Red & Green LEDs
FlexDIO (Ch 8-11): 5V pull-up for buttons & limit switches
PWM Headers (Ch 0-9): 50 Hz pulses for manipulator servos
slides.visual: Annotated photograph of VMX-pi pin headers.
slides.notes: Show students where each header is physically located on their robot.

slides.title: Junior Hands-On Challenge: Zero Wire Snags
bullets: Route CAN and power cables inside the U-channel cavity
Verify strain relief: wires must never pull taut
Maintain at least 20mm clearance from rotating wheels
slides.visual: Clean, spiral-wrapped cable harness running inside U-channel.
slides.notes: Grade student harnesses on clean routing and strain relief.

slides.title: Exit Ticket & Verification
bullets: Q1: Why does Linux need an FPGA coprocessor?
Q2: Why are CAN wires twisted together?
Q3: Which header drives status LEDs?
slides.visual: Exit ticket prompt and terminal status check.
slides.notes: Review candump terminal command output.

slides.title: Building the Robot Chassis
bullets: Constructing the physical 24cm x 18cm aluminum frame
Chassis squareness: why geometry prevents drift
Mounting plates, standoffs, and electronics deck
slides.visual: Assembled 24cm x 18cm robot chassis frame.
slides.notes: Emphasize that straight robot driving begins with a perfectly square mechanical frame.

slides.title: Chassis Blueprint & Target Dimensions
bullets: Length: 240 mm (24.0 cm) side channels
Width: 180 mm (18.0 cm) cross channels
Base Height Clearance: 100 mm (10.0 cm)
slides.visual: Dimensioned CAD drawing of the chassis frame.
slides.notes: Have students verify beam lengths with their steel rulers before assembling.

slides.title: The Parallelogram Trap
bullets: If corner angles deviate by even 1°, frame becomes a parallelogram
A skewed chassis will veer sideways even with identical motor speeds
Solution: The Pythagorean Diagonal Audit ($D = 300.0\,\text{mm}$)
slides.visual: Comparison diagram: Parallelogram distortion vs True Rectangle.
slides.notes: Explain why software odometry cannot fix a mechanically crooked chassis.

slides.title: Assembly Steps: Finger-Tight First
bullets: Step 1: Lay out channels with open U facing INWARD
Step 2: Insert M4x12mm bolts through corner gussets
Step 3: Thread Nyloc nuts finger-tight (allow frame to flex)
slides.visual: Exploded view of corner gusset, channel, M4 bolt, and Nyloc nut.
slides.notes: Stress the finger-tight rule: do not torque until measured.

slides.title: Diagonal Measurement Technique
bullets: Measure Diagonal A (Top-Left to Bottom-Right)
Measure Diagonal B (Top-Right to Bottom-Left)
Nudge frame until both diagonals match within ±0.5 mm!
slides.visual: Diagram showing diagonal measurement lines forming an 'X'.
slides.notes: Demonstrate holding the ruler firmly against the corner hole centers.

slides.title: Alternating Cross-Torquing Technique
bullets: Press frame firmly flat against table with palm
Torque corner bolts in an X-pattern (like lug nuts on a car)
Verifying flat stance: tap all four corners; zero rocking allowed!
slides.visual: Numbered diagram showing 1-2-3-4 tightening sequence.
slides.notes: Explain that tightening one side completely first will warp the frame.

slides.title: Junior Hands-On Challenge: The Caliper Audit
bullets: Teacher inspection: Caliper measure Length, Width, and Diagonals
Marble surface plate test: all four corners must touch flat
Passing Standard: Diagonal difference < 0.5 mm with zero rocking
slides.visual: Digital caliper measuring diagonal corner gusset holes.
slides.notes: Inspect and sign off each team's frame in their workbook.

slides.title: Exit Ticket & Cleanup
bullets: Q1: What are the target dimensions (L x W x H)?
Q2: Why must both diagonals match within 0.5mm?
Q3: What happens if a chassis is skewed into a parallelogram?
slides.visual: Exit ticket prompt.
slides.notes: Review submissions before dismissing.

slides.title: Installing Motors and Wheels
bullets: Maverick 12V DC Planetary Gearmotors (60:1 reduction)
Deriving the 1,680 Ticks/Rev Encoder Resolution
Mounting 100mm Rubber Drive Wheels & Rear Omni Caster
slides.visual: Maverick gearmotor with 100mm wheel attached.
slides.notes: Introduce today's transition from static frame to moving vehicle.

slides.title: Why Gear Reduction? Torque vs. Speed
bullets: Bare DC motors spin at 6,000+ RPM but produce tiny torque
60:1 Planetary Gearbox reduces speed to 100 RPM
Output torque is multiplied by 60x to haul payloads and climb ramps
slides.visual: Cutaway diagram of a multi-stage planetary gearbox.
slides.notes: Explain the mechanical trade-off: speed is traded for immense pushing force.

slides.title: Quadrature Encoders: 1680 Ticks Per Turn
bullets: 28 raw magnetic pulses per motor shaft turn
$28 \times 60\text{ (gear ratio)} = 1,680\text{ ticks per full wheel turn}$
Wheel circumference: $C = \pi \times 100\,\text{mm} \approx 314.16\,\text{mm}$
Resolution: $314.16 / 1680 \approx 0.187\,\text{mm per tick}$!
slides.visual: Quadrature wave diagram (Channel A and B 90° out of phase).
slides.notes: Walk through the math step-by-step on the board. Make sure every student writes 1680 in their book.

slides.title: D-Shaft Flat Alignment & Blue Threadlocker
bullets: Motor shaft has one flat face (6mm D-Shaft)
Set screw MUST be tightened perpendicular to the flat face
Always apply one drop of blue threadlocker (Loctite 242)
slides.visual: Diagram showing set screw clamping squarely onto flat face of D-shaft.
slides.notes: Show students what happens if set screw hits the curved side: it slips instantly under load.

slides.title: Mounting Drive Wheels & Rear Caster
bullets: Secure clamping motor mounts to side rails with M4 bolts
Fasten 100mm wheels with four M3 screws in cross pattern
Attach rear omni caster ball and adjust spacers for level stance
slides.visual: Chassis side view showing drive wheels and rear omni caster.
slides.notes: Ensure 1mm clearance gap between wheel hub and channel wall.

slides.title: Wiring Harness to Titan M0 & M1
bullets: Left Motor harness → Titan Motor 0 (M0) & Encoder 0 (ENC0)
Right Motor harness → Titan Motor 1 (M1) & Encoder 1 (ENC1)
Track width: $W = 200\,\text{mm}$ (center-to-center wheel distance)
slides.visual: Titan Quad connector diagram with M0 and M1 harnesses plugged in.
slides.notes: Verify harness colors match port labels on the Titan.

slides.title: Junior Hands-On Challenge: Roll-Out Test
bullets: Place robot on a gentle 5° ramp with motors unplugged
Robot must roll down straight without veering
Listen for smooth mechanical hum: zero grinding or binding!
slides.visual: Robot rolling down test ramp.
slides.notes: If a robot veers, check for tire rubbing or uneven caster height.

slides.title: Exit Ticket & Derivation Check
bullets: Q1: What is the gear reduction ratio?
Q2: Calculate encoder ticks: $28 \times 60 = ?$
Q3: Why do we apply blue threadlocker?
slides.visual: Exit ticket prompt.
slides.notes: Sign off student calculation tables in Worksheet 04.

slides.title: Power and Wiring Hygiene
bullets: Wiring the 12V DC power loop: battery, fuse, and switch
Segregated power rails: Muscle (Titan) vs. Brain (VMX)
Mandatory Multimeter Polarity Audit (+12V verification)
slides.visual: Complete robot power wiring diagram.
slides.notes: Today we bring the robot to life! Electrical safety is our highest priority.

slides.title: Power Topology: Preventing Brownouts
bullets: Motors pull up to 20A peak during acceleration
Brownout danger: sudden current spike crashes the Raspberry Pi
Solution: Segregated power tree with regulated auxiliary logic supply
slides.visual: Block diagram: Battery → Fuse → Switch → Titan VIN & VMX Regulated In.
slides.notes: Explain why motors and microprocessors must never share thin, unregulated wires.

slides.title: Circuit Protection: The 20A Blade Fuse
bullets: Automotive 20A yellow blade fuse in positive (Red) wire
Sacrificial element: melts in milliseconds if a short circuit occurs
Protects battery pack against fire and prevents melted wiring
slides.visual: Cutaway diagram of blade fuse showing internal metal bridge.
slides.notes: Pass around a blown fuse vs a good fuse so students know how to visually inspect it.

slides.title: Reverse Polarity Danger: The XT60 Guardian
bullets: Reversing Red (+) and Black (-) destroys the Titan H-Bridge in 5 ms
Yellow XT60 connectors are physically keyed with chamfered corners
Never force a connector backward!
slides.visual: Cross-section of XT60 connector showing keyed chamfered profile.
slides.notes: Emphasize: never solder or wire battery leads backward. Yellow XT60 only plugs in one way.

slides.title: Step-by-Step Power Wiring Procedure
bullets: Step 1: Insert 20A blade fuse into inline rubber holder
Step 2: Mount heavy-duty toggle switch to rear bracket (UP = ON)
Step 3: Strip 6mm wire and clamp into Titan VIN (+) and GND (-)
slides.visual: Close-up of Titan power screw terminals with Red and Black leads.
slides.notes: Ensure copper is clamped under screw head, not plastic insulation jacket.

slides.title: The Mandatory Multimeter Polarity Audit
bullets: Black probe on Titan GND (-), Red probe on Titan VIN (+)
Multimeter must read between +12.0V and +13.5V DC
A minus sign (-12V) means wires are REVERSED! Do not turn ON!
slides.visual: Multimeter display showing +12.6V DC reading.
slides.notes: Every single team must have their multimeter reading signed off by the teacher before turning switch ON.

slides.title: Junior Hands-On Challenge: The 5G Tug & Shake
bullets: Gently tug every wire: zero wires may slip from terminals
Shake robot vertically and horizontally: zero rattles
Turn ON: confirm solid green power LEDs on both controllers!
slides.visual: Instructor performing tug test on robot wiring.
slides.notes: Celebrate this milestone! The students' physical robot is officially complete.

slides.title: Exit Ticket & Module 1 Graduation!
bullets: Q1: What happens if battery polarity is reversed?
Q2: What is the purpose of the 20A blade fuse?
Q3: Why are motor and sensor wires routed separately?
Congratulations on completing Module 1: Build Your First Robot!
slides.visual: Graduation banner with robot completion badge.
slides.notes: Issue Module 1 completion stamps and prepare for Module 2: Connect and Drive!
